name: Schedule posts from a Notion content database with Socialync

parameters.content:
### How it works
Write your posts in a Notion database and let this workflow send them out. Every hour it takes the first page whose Status is Ready. The page gives the caption, the platforms, the time and an optional image or video. The page changes to Scheduling first, so no later run can take it again. Socialync schedules the post, and the page changes to Scheduled with the post ID in Notes. A page with a problem changes to Needs fixing with the reason, so your team sees it where they work.

Posts are scheduled without a manual approval step. You can cancel or change any scheduled post in Socialync until it goes out.

### Setup
1. Create an API key at https://socialync.io/go/n8n-node-keys and add it as a Socialync credential.
2. Add a Notion credential and share your database with the integration.
3. Give the database these properties: Name (title), Caption (text), Platforms (multi select or text), Publish at (date), Image (files), Video URL (url), Status (status with Ready, Scheduling, Scheduled and Needs fixing), Notes (text).
4. Choose the database in the Notion node and set your time zone in Settings.

### Customization
A date with no time posts at 9am in your time zone. Leave Platforms empty to use the list in Settings. YouTube needs the page title. TikTok needs a privacy level in Settings.

A page stuck on Scheduling means a run stopped part way. Check Socialync, then set the page to Scheduled or Ready.

API reference: https://socialync.io/go/n8n-node

parameters.content:
## Pick a page
Every hour, take the first page with Status Ready. A date with no time posts at 9am.

## Check the page
The page needs a caption and valid links. A problem goes back to Notes.

## Schedule it
The page is set to Scheduling first. Socialync then schedules the post and Notion shows the post ID.

## Status property
Status must be a Notion status property with Ready, Scheduling, Scheduled and Needs fixing. Without Scheduling, nothing is posted.
